identity.name: AWS S3 Mass-Object Exfiltration by a Suspicious Identity — Cortex Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1530)
identity.summary: One IAM identity issues a high-volume burst of s3:GetObject calls reading objects from a bucket from a new source — the CloudTrail shape of bulk cloud-storage theft. No single GetObject is known-bad; the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the mass-download deviation from the identity's learned object-access baseline, anchored to the suspicious-identity causality chain.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the user, endpoint, and network behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the CLOUD / CDR plane against S3 mass-object exfiltration — the bulk data-theft pattern where a stolen, exposed, or over-privileged identity reads a bucket's objects wholesale. Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud ingests the AWS CloudTrail audit stream (normalised to cloud_audit_logs, with S3 data events enabled) and learns each identity's object-access baseline — which principals read which buckets, how many reads, at what rate. This scenario streams shape-true CloudTrail S3 data-event records via the cloud_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer (provider=aws, event_pattern storage_object_download): a high-volume burst of s3:GetObject calls on one bucket, all from a single suspicious identity and an anomalous source IP. Two ABIOCs — named for the exact Cortex XSIAM analytics alerts they exercise ('Suspicious identity downloaded multiple objects from a bucket' and 'An identity performed a suspicious download of multiple cloud storage objects') — fire on the mass-download deviation. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a single API name would miss this: every s3:GetObject is a legitimate call an application makes constantly. The catch comes from the read-volume deviation from the identity's learned object-access baseline plus the causality chain (one identity -> high-volume GetObject read burst on one bucket from a new source), not a known-bad signature. Supporting validation XQL confirms the emitted S3 read events landed in cloud_audit_logs and surfaces the per-identity GetObject read burst; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single mass-object-exfiltration incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex behavioral analytics caught bulk cloud-storage theft no static rule was written for.

actors.name: Opportunistic cloud intruders abusing stolen, exposed, or over-privileged identities to bulk-download S3 data

campaigns: Cloud data-exfiltration via suspicious-identity S3 mass download — high-volume GetObject read burst (2022-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-019 — AWS S3 mass-object exfiltration by a suspicious identity (GetObject download fan-out) for Cortex ABIOC validation via the cloud_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR ingesting the AWS CloudTrail audit stream (with S3 data events enabled) into cloud_audit_logs so per-identity object access is profiled.

An operator-supplied HTTP collector (XSIAM Broker VM HTTP applet / native collector / Cribl or nginx forwarder) already wired into Cortex as a CloudTrail source, reachable at COLLECTOR_URL and on the campaign target_allowlist.

payload.code:
# No real AWS mutation. Stream shape-true CloudTrail S3 data-event records via the
# cloud_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer: a high-volume burst of s3:GetObject
# calls on one bucket, all from a single suspicious identity and an anomalous
# source IP.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:=https://collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/logs/v1/event}"
: "${COLLECTOR_HOST:=collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid}"
cat > /tmp/cdr-019-s3-exfil.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-CDR-019
name: "CDR — AWS S3 mass-object exfiltration by a suspicious identity"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - "$COLLECTOR_HOST"
dry_run: false
steps:
  - step_id: step-01
    plugin: cloud_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "$COLLECTOR_URL"
      provider: aws
      event_pattern: storage_object_download
      burst_count: 60
      iterations: 1
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/cdr-019-s3-exfil.yml --live

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator-supplied HTTP collector URL already wired into Cortex as a CloudTrail source.

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_HOST
input_variables.description: Hostname of the collector, added to the campaign target_allowlist.

expected_artifacts.description: A high-volume burst of CloudTrail s3:GetObject data events from one identity on a single bucket.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: eventName = "GetObject" and count() of GetObject calls within 5m exceeds the identity learned object-access baseline

cleanup.code: rm -f /tmp/cdr-019-s3-exfil.yml; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-019 cleanup complete — synthetic CloudTrail records only; no real AWS object was read or moved.'

abiocs.name: Suspicious identity downloaded multiple objects from a bucket
abiocs.description: A single IAM identity whose learned Cortex object-access baseline is a small, steady read of a handful of S3 objects suddenly issues a high-volume burst of s3:GetObject calls on one bucket, from a source new for that identity. The ABIOC anchors the mass-download deviation to the causality chain (suspicious identity -> GetObject read burst on one bucket) rather than to any single API name, catching bulk cloud-storage theft a static rule keyed on GetObject would drown in noise on.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName = "GetObject"
| filter isnull(errorCode)
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 300)
| comp count() as object_downloads by userIdentityArn, bucket_name, sourceIPAddress
| filter object_downloads >= 50
| sort desc object_downloads
| fields userIdentityArn, bucket_name, sourceIPAddress, object_downloads
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-identity S3 object-access baseline (a few reads on known buckets) -> suspicious identity -> high-volume s3:GetObject read burst on one bucket from a source IP/user-agent new for this identity, anchored to that identity.

abiocs.name: An identity performed a suspicious download of multiple cloud storage objects
abiocs.description: An identity issues an anomalously high volume of s3:GetObject reads on one bucket, far above its learned per-bucket access volume. Every read is a legitimate call; the ABIOC fires on the read-volume deviation from the identity's learned cloud-storage behavior, anchored to the high-volume download burst on the same bucket.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName = "GetObject"
| filter isnull(errorCode)
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| comp count() as objects_read by userIdentityArn, bucket_name
| filter objects_read >= 50
| sort desc objects_read
| fields userIdentityArn, bucket_name, objects_read
abiocs.causality_anchor: Assumed/IAM identity -> high-volume s3:GetObject read burst on one bucket, anchored to the identity that first exhibited the mass download.

xql_queries.name: SIM-CDR-019 S3 GetObject Burst Surfaced in Cloud Audit Log
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName = "GetObject"
| comp count() as s3_read_events by userIdentityArn, bucket_name
| filter s3_read_events >= 1
| sort desc s3_read_events
| fields userIdentityArn, bucket_name, s3_read_events

xql_queries.name: SIM-CDR-019 Suspicious-Identity Download Fan-Out By Bucket
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName = "GetObject"
| comp count() as object_downloads by userIdentityArn, bucket_name, sourceIPAddress
| filter object_downloads >= 1
| sort desc object_downloads
| fields userIdentityArn, bucket_name, sourceIPAddress, object_downloads

correlation_rules.name: Mass Object Exfiltration — Suspicious-Identity Download Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Suspicious identity downloaded multiple objects from a bucket) AND ABIOC(An identity performed a suspicious download of multiple cloud storage objects) — fuses the two auto-tuned mass-download deviations on the same identity and bucket within the run window into a single S3 mass-object-exfiltration incident anchored to the suspicious-identity causality chain.

use_cases.name: AWS S3 Mass-Object Exfiltration Detection via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: Cortex auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn each identity's per-bucket S3 object-access baseline and detect bulk cloud-storage theft — a suspicious identity issuing a high-volume s3:GetObject read burst on a bucket — anchored to the suspicious-identity mass-download causality chain, where no static rule was written for the legitimate GetObject calls involved.

test_cases.objective: Cortex learns the per-identity S3 object-access baseline and an injected mass-download burst fires both ABIOCs and the correlation.
preconditions: Cortex Cloud / CDR ingesting the AWS CloudTrail audit stream with S3 data events enabled.
Baseline window elapsed with identities reading only their narrow, known object set.
steps: Stream a high-volume burst of s3:GetObject calls on one bucket from a single suspicious identity via cloud_audit_emitter (event_pattern storage_object_download).
Observe both ABIOCs fire on the mass-download deviation.
Observe CR-CDR-0019 raise one stitched mass-object-exfiltration incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Suspicious identity downloaded multiple objects from a bucket` fires.
ABIOC `An identity performed a suspicious download of multiple cloud storage objects` fires.
Correlation CR-CDR-0019 raises one stitched S3 mass-object-exfiltration incident.

preventive_controls: Scope S3 access to least privilege with bucket policies and IAM conditions so a single identity cannot bulk-read an entire bucket.
Enable S3 data events in CloudTrail (or S3 server-access logging) so per-object GetObject reads are observable to Cortex.
Prefer short-lived credentials and rotate aggressively; apply an SCP / permissions boundary denying broad s3:GetObject to workload identities that need only a fixed key set.
Enable S3 Block Public Access and require VPC-endpoint or known-source access so downloads from anomalous IPs are denied outright.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-identity per-bucket object-access baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules on GetObject.
Alert on an identity whose s3:GetObject read count on a bucket spikes above its learned baseline within a short window.
Alert on an identity issuing a high-volume s3:GetObject read burst on a single bucket from a source new for that identity.
